correctness.rationale: For every m>=1, the right-preconditioned affine companion has Krylov space span(e_1,...,e_m). Its (m+1)-by-m least-squares matrix has a one-dimensional nullspace of its transpose. Direct orthogonal projection produces the stated R_m squared identity; its first two residual coordinates then give the exact recovered scalar residual. The m=1 boundary is handled by v_2=0. Geometric sums prove all three asymptotic cases and the exceptional nonzero outside-disk lifted floor. A separate exact-rational companion least-squares verifier passed 175 parameter/dimension comparisons plus a symbolic limiting identity. No finite enumeration substitutes for the all-m proof.

value.rationale: The published nonvanishing companion-residual bound raises a natural concrete question: does it force failure to solve the original problem? The theorem gives an exact all-m answer and a sharp parameter-specific failure of that inference, with a physical residual identically zero even though the companion residual can stagnate near 1/sqrt(2). The three s regimes and exact cancellation locus give a usable diagnostic for evaluating stopping criteria and expansion-coordinate scaling. It is a motivated structural boundary of a recently analyzed algorithm, not an arbitrary numerical slice; it does not claim general matrix implications.
